mappings._comment: The export modal and the PNG/CSV writers behind it: every spec that opens the export modal.
ScheduleInterval is shared by ingestion, data quality, data contracts, and application configuration, so changes must exercise every scheduler-facing flow.

The agents tab has to keep listing agents, and keep its run history readable, while the pipeline-service status call is slow or failing — only the controls that reach that service may go down with it. These are the files that decide it. The spec stubs the status endpoint and carries no ingestion tag, so chromium alone is enough; it needs no Airflow fixture.

The application config forms are built from the UI-local application schemas by ApplicationsClassBase, and the Search Indexing form additionally fills its entity picker from GET /v1/search/entityTypes. The Settings/** entry above selects no spec that actually opens an app config form, so a change to the schemas, the loader, or the endpoint that fills them shipped unrun — the SearchIndexApplication entity-picker locator broke once the server-driven list gained tableColumn and nothing caught it.

FilterSelect replaced SearchDropdown as the quick-filter renderer, so the generated map (which only walks openmetadata-ui spec imports) no longer routes filter dropdown changes to the former SearchDropdown consumer specs. Mirror that consumer set for the core component and its Dropdown base so a FilterSelect change selects the Explore/lineage/Test Definition/bulk-operation coverage on the PR instead of the merge queue.

Same service sources as above, but these two specs carry PLAYWRIGHT_INGESTION_TAG_OBJ, so they only run in the Ingestion project. Listing them under chromium/Basic selects them but the shard planner drops them.

The landing-page Activity Feed widget is driven by ActivityFeedProvider and feedsAPI, and is exercised by specs that none of these paths live in. Without this entry a widget change selected only the specs it edited directly, and a broken filter reached the merge queue before any of these ran.

What reaches an entity's activity feed is decided server-side: the ActivityFeedAlert seed filter and the repository that builds and lists activity events (an asset's feed includes its data contract's).

The customize-landing-page and widget-filter playwright helpers are shared by every landing-page/customization spec. Without this entry a helper-only change (e.g. a wait fix in customizeLandingPage.ts or widgetFilters.ts) counted as an unmapped file, so CustomizeWidgets/CustomizeLandingPage and the other specs that execute the changed helpers never ran on the PR. Specs listed are the exact importers of these modules; DataInsight.spec.ts runs in the Data Insight project.

The persona-driven home page: its shell, the topic-card widgets and the hooks that feed them. Every card has its behaviour spec under Features/LandingPageWidgets; CustomizeWidgets and CustomizeLandingPage drive the same cards through the persona layout editor. The landing-page fixture is listed because every spec in that folder signs in through it.
Persona AI Context moved from Persona settings to Context Center. Cover its page, route, API, and shared Playwright navigation so a relocation cannot leave its E2E suites out of targeted CI.

Metric page, custom-metric page, bulk-edit grid, and the CSV import/export machinery all funnel through this cluster. MetricBulkImportExportEdit + BulkImport + ClassificationImportExport have been ejecting PRs from the merge queue because none of them named these paths — PR CI skipped them entirely and the queue was the first place they ran. The two playwright helpers are included so a wait/selector fix in importUtils.ts also routes back to the specs that consume it.

The bulk-edit grid renders tier and other popover cell editors from CSVUtilsClassBase, and the tier editor is TierCard. TierCard alone mapped only to TierWidget, so a TierCard-only change skipped the bulk-edit tier step in DataAssetRulesDisabled, which first failed in the merge queue (#33987).

The certification picker renders on entity headers, the Domain/Data Product certification widget, the bulk-edit grid's certification cell and the workflow Set Action form; KeyDownStopPropagationWrapper wraps the grid's popover cell editors. The generated map routed none of them, so a change ran the full suite.
Column bulk operations and column sorting exercise the ColumnBulkOperations page and columnAPI; keeps ColumnBulkOperationsTagsGlossary tied to both this and the Tag mapping above.

Customize pages (Details and AppMode sidebar) plus the customizable-widgets component tree feed the CustomizeDetailPage and CustomizeNavigation specs. Data Insight is included because the customize flow ships a data-insight preview.
Default glossary and glossary-term page layouts and their widget registry. Persona customization edits these layouts, and the glossary pages render them.
Container entity page. Container.spec.ts covers the storage-container details view and had no mapping before this entry.

AppMode covers the ai-shell / admin-shell split. Sources are spread across the AppModeSwitcher, the ai-shell platform tree (routing + sidebar), the Settings AppMode pages, and the appModeSession util. The generated appModePreference schema is included because a schema change ripples into every AppMode spec that reads a persisted preference.
AI-mode settings modal, Platform Settings panel (the modal home of the classic Settings > Preferences pages).
AI-mode settings modal, Preferences panel (theme incl. system, compact sidebar, language) and the shared theme/sidebar state it drives.
System announcements: Settings > Notifications > Announcements (list, form, routed pages) and its AI-mode settings-modal section.
Announcement pieces shared by system announcements and asset announcements: the REST client, the add/edit modal and its date field, and the drawer list with its delete dialog.
Shared shell of the AI-mode settings modal: the nav registry, its ids and the section/row layout every panel renders. A change here can move or restyle any panel, so every modal spec runs.
Settings modal Bots panel: list, add form, detail and token section.
Settings modal Notifications panel: alert list, alert form and detail views.
Settings modal Applications panel: installed apps, marketplace and install flow.
Settings modal Governance panel: glossary term relations and intake forms.
Settings modal Personas panel: persona list, detail and customize views.
Settings modal Custom Properties panel.
Logged-in user permissions and their loading state, read by the settings modal's admin-only and permission-gated surfaces.
FormBuilderV1 renders every app-config, SSO, ingestion and service-connection form, so it runs the specs those forms map to.
SSO configuration form and its tests; the form itself is also mapped by the generated map.
Shared data-asset picker (shell, rows, footer, count bar, async options hook) behind both DataAssetSelectList and DataAssetAsyncSelectList.
Legacy RJSF FormBuilder and its JSONSchema widgets, used only by the application config, app run history and SSO configuration forms.

Backend integration tests are a test-only Maven module — not packaged into the server the suite runs against, nor into the UI bundle — so no change here can alter a spec outcome. Mapped to no specs rather than left unmapped: openmetadata-integration-tests/ is in UNMAPPED_CODE_ROOTS, so without this every backend-IT change escalates to a full-suite run.
The Data Contract tab: its add/edit forms, contract cards and their utils. Every contract spec drives these forms, and the ODCS specs edit imported contracts through them.

The ESLint suppressions baseline is read only by the linter: it ships in neither the server nor the UI bundle, so no change to it can alter a spec outcome. Mapped to no specs rather than left unmapped, so pruning it does not escalate to a full-suite run.

The AI-mode Data Quality Test Cases tab (list, filters, soft delete and restore). The generated map reaches only the shared classic components it renders, so a change to the AI-mode tab itself would otherwise run the full suite.

ConfirmationModal, its props and unit test. The generated map sends ConfirmationModal.tsx to the first three specs (through its testIds); TestSuiteDetailsPage.spec.ts is added because it asserts the destructive confirm on bulk remove.

The AI-mode bundle test suite page and its test case search. TestSuiteDetailsPage.spec.ts runs the suite search in Classic and AI mode; the generated map reaches only the shared classic components it renders.
The AI-mode test case Run now / Retry controls. Only the AI-mode detail page and the run execution error banner render them, so the generated map does not reach them.

The test case detail page header and its Deleted badge (Classic and AI mode). TestCaseSoftDeleteRestore is the only spec asserting the badge, and the generated map skips the deleted-badge test id (too many owners).

The limit banner shows only once a resource limit is reached, and only Collate enables the limits config that sets one, so no spec in this suite can display it. Mapped to no specs rather than left unmapped, so a change to it does not escalate to a full-suite run.

The Add/Edit Test Definition drawer and the Test Library pages that open it, in classic and AI mode. The generated map reaches only TestDefinitionFormBody (through its testIds), so a change to the drawer shell, its props or the AI-mode page would otherwise run the full suite.

The first-login welcome screen and the post-deploy upgrade screen (the chunk-load ErrorFallback), with the brand hooks and artwork they render. WelcomeScreen.spec.ts drives the welcome screen in classic and AI mode (shown once, close, both actions, stays dismissed on the kept-alive AI home); AppModeAiPersonaLandsAtRoot.spec.ts covers the AI-mode landing route the gate wraps. No spec forces a chunk-load failure, so the upgrade screen is covered by ErrorFallback.test.tsx.

Mode-aware settings links (ADR:2026-10-21-settings-pages-are-classic-only): the path-to-modal-hash map, the route builders (pure paths) and the call sites that wrap them in getSettingsLink, and the hash router that opens the settings modal from a pushed link. Classic keeps its paths, so the classic settings specs whose links these builders produce run too.
Settings-modal Members and Access Control panels, including the per-view permission gates that mirror classic SettingsRouter (ADR:2026-10-21-settings-pages-are-classic-only).
AI-mode observability alert pages (list, details, add/edit drawer) and the alert kind they serve.
Breadcrumbs of the classic Add KPI, Add Role and Add Policy pages.
AI-mode Inbox (routed /inbox page): activity and task lists and their item components.

The Lineage section of the entity summary panel (Upstream/Downstream counts). ExplorePageRightPanel.spec.ts opens the panel and navigates from its lineage section; the data product Assets tab renders the same panel.

Service Insights widgets and their empty-state placeholders. Pagination.spec.ts and ServiceEntityPermissions.spec.ts open a service's Insights tab; ConnectionServiceDetails.spec.ts covers it in AI mode.
The shared page pagers. Pagination.spec.ts and GlobalPageSize.spec.ts drive Next/Previous and the page size across list pages; the components' importers map them further.

The Context Center icon in the classic left sidebar (also the Context Center asset and knowledge-page logo). Navbar.spec.ts walks the classic sidebar that renders it; its stroke weight is otherwise only visible to the visual-regression baselines.
